title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #765 asks for the growth rate of ex(n; C₄), the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph with no 4-cycle. Answer: ex(n; C₄) ~ (1/2)n^{3/2}. Solved through contributions from Erdős-Klein (1938), Reiman (1958), Erdős-Rényi-Brown, and Füredi (1983). Erdős's refined conjecture about lower-order terms was disproved by Ma-Yang (2023).

title: 4-Cycle and C₄-Free Definitions
content: A 4-cycle (C₄) consists of four distinct vertices v₁, v₂, v₃, v₄ forming a cycle v₁-v₂-v₃-v₄-v₁. A graph is C₄-free (isFourCycleFree) if it contains no such subgraph. Equivalently, no two vertices share more than one common neighbor.

title: Extremal Function ex(n; C₄)
content: The extremal number ex_C4(n) is axiomatized as the maximum edges in an n-vertex C₄-free graph. Unlike the original placeholder (= 0), this is now a proper axiom with ex_C4_realized guaranteeing existence of an optimal C₄-free graph.

title: Historical Bounds
content: Three key bounds axiomatized: (1) Erdős-Klein 1938: ex(n;C₄) = O(n^{3/2}), proved via double counting of 2-paths. (2) Reiman 1958: the limit L = lim ex(n;C₄)/n^{3/2} satisfies 1/(2√2) ≤ L ≤ 1/2. (3) Erdős-Rényi-Brown: projective plane PG(2,q) gives ex(n;C₄) ≥ (1/2)q(q+1)² for n = q²+q+1.

title: Main Theorem: ex(n;C₄) ~ (1/2)n^{3/2}
content: The asymptotic formula is axiomatized and the main theorem erdos_765 is proved by direct application. For all ε > 0, there exists N such that |ex(n;C₄)/n^{3/2} - 1/2| < ε for n ≥ N. This answers Erdős Problem #765.

title: Füredi's Exact Result (1983)
content: For q > 13 a prime power and n = q²+q+1: ex(n;C₄) = (1/2)q(q+1)² exactly. The projective plane construction is optimal for large q. This gives exact values for infinitely many n, not just asymptotic bounds.

title: Erdős's Conjecture and Ma-Yang Disproof
content: Erdős conjectured ex(n;C₄) = (1/2)n^{3/2} + (1/4)n + O(√n). Ma-Yang (2023) disproved this: for a positive density of n, the coefficient 1/4 can be improved to 1/4-c for some c > 0. The ma_yang_disproof axiom formalizes this with a meaningful type signature involving positive density sets.

title: B₂ Sequences (Sidon Sets)
content: A set A ⊆ ℕ is a B₂ sequence if all pairwise sums a+b (a≤b) are distinct. Erdős discovered ex(n;C₄) = O(n^{3/2}) in 1936 while studying B₂ sequences (Problem #425), five years before Turán's systematic study of extremal graph theory.

title: Projective Plane Examples
content: Four projective plane vertex counts proved: PG(2,2)=7 (Fano plane), PG(2,3)=13, PG(2,4)=21, PG(2,5)=31. Each uses the formula q²+q+1 and is proved by simp+ring. These are the C₄-free extremal graph constructions.

title: Summary Theorem
content: erdos_765_summary combines the asymptotic formula (via axiom) and the Fano plane computation (proved by simp+ring). Problem #765 is SOLVED: ex(n;C₄) ~ (1/2)n^{3/2}.
